results.answer: The provided sources do not include NVIDIA’s total revenue for fiscal year 2021. They cover fiscal years 2019 and 2024, plus quarters of fiscal year 2025. [Source 1] [Source 2] [Source 3] [Source 4] [Source 5]

Meta’s total revenue in the first quarter of 2022 is not provided in the sources. The sources cover fiscal 2023, Q1 2024, Q1 2025, and Q2 2026, but not Q1 2022. [Source 1] [Source 2] [Source 3] [Source 4] [Source 5]

The sources do not provide Tesla’s full-year 2024 total-revenue result, so they do not establish that total revenues fell for the entire year.

For the **nine months ended September 30, 2024**, automotive sales revenue decreased **$4.06 billion, or 7%**, primarily because of lower average selling prices from price reductions and attractive financing, as well as mix. Tesla also reported a decrease of approximately **17,000 combined Model 3 and Model Y cash deliveries**, partly related to the early production ramp of the updated Model 3. [Source 1]

The decline was partly offset by higher revenue from other areas: in the nine-month period, automotive regulatory credits revenue increased **$714 million, or 53%**, and services and other revenue increased **$1.53 billion, or 25%**. [Source 2] In Q3 specifically, automotive sales revenue actually increased **$249 million, or 1%**, so the available sources do not support describing every quarter of 2024 as a revenue decline. [Source 1]
